fields.test_cases_present: partial - the spec lists protocol requirements that can be turned into compliance test scenarios but does not provide a formal test plan.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Reset behavior
scenarios: ARESETn asserted asynchronously; all VALID signals must be LOW during reset.
ARESETn deasserted on rising ACLK; VALID may only assert at the next rising ACLK edge after ARESETn=HIGH.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: VALID/READY handshake compliance
scenarios: Source asserts VALID and holds info stable until READY (no premature retract).
Destination asserts READY ahead of VALID; transfer occurs in one cycle when VALID arrives.
Both assert same cycle.
Source does NOT wait for READY before VALID.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: FIXED burst with WSTRB variation per beat (FIFO emulation).
scenarios: AxBURST=0b00 with same AxADDR each beat; WSTRB varies.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: INCR burst aligned/unaligned/length 1..256
scenarios: 32-bit transfers on 32-bit bus, address 0x00, length 4 (aligned).
32-bit transfers on 32-bit bus, address 0x01 (unaligned), length 4.
32-bit transfers on 64-bit bus, address 0x07, length 5 (unaligned, partial first beat).
AXI4 INCR length up to 256.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: WRAP burst at cache-line boundaries
scenarios: WRAP length must be one of 2,4,8,16.
Start address must be aligned to AxSIZE.
Address wraps to Wrap_Boundary when reaching upper bound.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: 4KB boundary enforcement
scenarios: Burst that would cross a 4KB boundary must be rejected/split by master; no slave may receive such a burst.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: WLAST/RLAST correctness
scenarios: WLAST must assert exactly once, on the final write beat.
RLAST must assert exactly once, on the final read beat.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: In-order completion for same-ID transactions
scenarios: Issue two reads with same ARID; RID must echo and responses must arrive in issue order.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Out-of-order completion for different IDs
scenarios: Issue two reads with different ARID; slave may complete in any order.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Exclusive access read-modify-write
scenarios: Exclusive read followed by exclusive write from same master with matching ID at same address -> EXOKAY.
Exclusive read; another master writes; exclusive write -> OKAY (fail) with no memory update.
Exclusive access to slave that does not support -> OKAY for both phases.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Error response handling
scenarios: SLVERR for unsupported transfer / read-only-location write / timeout.
DECERR from default slave for undecoded address.
Error must still complete required number of beats (no early termination).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Inactive byte lanes
scenarios: WSTRB LOW for byte lanes that don't carry valid data; recommended WDATA=0 for inactive lanes.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Deadlock avoidance
scenarios: Master must not wait for AWREADY before driving WVALID (would deadlock if slave waits for WVALID first).
Slave VALID must not be combinationally dependent on its incoming READY.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: AXI4 BVALID waits for AW + W + WLAST
scenarios: AXI4/AXI5 slave must not assert BVALID until both AW and W handshakes complete and WLAST is seen.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: AXI4 write data interleaving forbidden
scenarios: AXI4+ master must issue write data in the address-channel order; no WID interleaving.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Default values when optional signals omitted
scenarios: AWBURST absent -> assume INCR.
AWSIZE absent -> assume data bus width.
WSTRB absent -> assume all ones.

evidence.quote: A write response must always follow the last write transfer in a write transaction. Read data must always follow the read address of the data.

The dependency rules must be observed to prevent a deadlock condition. For example, a master must not wait for AWREADY to be asserted before driving WVALID. A deadlock condition can occur if the slave is waiting for WVALID before asserting AWREADY.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary. Early termination of bursts is not supported.

If a master attempts an exclusive read from a slave that does not support exclusive accesses, the slave returns the OKAY response instead of the EXOKAY response. ... The master can treat the OKAY response as an error condition indicating that the exclusive access is not supported.
The AXI protocol requires that all data transfers for a transaction are completed, even if an error condition occurs. Any component giving a DECERR response must meet this requirement.
